appraisal_events.evidence: je l'ai vu, vous savez, chez moi, éblouissant, à se mettre à genoux devant ; eh bien ! chez les autres, ce n'est plus le même homme, il n'a plus d'esprit, il faut lui arracher les mots, il est même ennuyeux
appraisal_events.explanation: Mme Verdurin backhandedly diminishes Brichot by claiming his brilliance exists only at her house and that he is dull elsewhere, while implicitly touting her own salon's power; the narrator's 'dit modestement' ironically flags this as self-flattery rather than a neutral observation.

appraisal_events.evidence: Un genre d'esprit comme celui de Brichot aurait été tenu pour stupidité pure dans la coterie où Swann avait passé sa jeunesse, bien qu'il soit compatible avec une intelligence réelle... Swann ne put trouver les plaisanteries de Brichot que pédantesques, vulgaires et grasses à écœurer... peut-être avait-il surtout perdu, ce soir-là, de son indulgence, en voyant l'amabilité que Mme Verdurin déployait pour ce Forcheville
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator exposes Swann's contemptuous judgment of Brichot as the product of his own class-conditioned taste rather than genuine discernment, and suggests it was compounded by jealous irritation at Mme Verdurin's warmth toward Forcheville, whom Odette had brought.

status_effects.explanation: She claims unique credit for bringing out Brichot's brilliance, locally elevating her salon's prestige through this self-serving comparison.
His wit is portrayed as inconsistent and dependent on venue, undercutting his independent stature as merely 'ennuyeux' elsewhere.
His scornful verdict on Brichot's humor is revealed as parochial bias inherited from his aristocratic milieu rather than genuine discernment.
His irritability is tied to jealous discomfort at seeing Mme Verdurin's amiability toward Forcheville, whom Odette had chosen to bring.

ambiguities: The narrator's explanation for Swann's harshness ('peut-être avait-il surtout perdu... de son indulgence') is hedged as speculative, leaving some uncertainty about how much of his negative judgment reflects genuine taste versus displaced jealousy over Forcheville.
